keywords.term: not all it's cracked up to be
keywords.def: (idiom) not as good as (many) people say it is
start again after a rest, so that you feel better about life
information collected from watching people's natural behaviour without interfering in it
(idiom) reject something because you think that it's not good enough for you

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是 BBC Learning English 的《6分钟英语》。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. In winter, people find different ways of keeping warm, like wearing extra clothes or staying indoors, but in some countries there's another way of keeping the cold out – going for a sauna.
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Georgie。在冬天，人们会用不同的方式来保暖，比如多穿衣服或待在室内，但在一些国家，还有另一种御寒的方法——蒸桑拿。

sentences.en: Yes, Nordic countries like Sweden and Finland have a long history of taking saunas, but now they're popping up in Britain too.
sentences.zh: 是的，像瑞典和芬兰这样的北欧国家有着悠久的桑拿历史，但现在它们在英国也开始流行起来了。

sentences.en: Have you ever been for a sauna, Georgie?
sentences.zh: Georgie，你蒸过桑拿吗？

sentences.en: I have, yes. And if I'm honest, I'm not a huge fan.
sentences.zh: 蒸过，是的。说实话，我不是很喜欢。

sentences.en: I don't really like being too hot. It's uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 我不太喜欢太热的感觉。很不舒服。

sentences.en: What about you, Neil? Oh really? I quite like a sauna.
sentences.zh: 你呢，Neil？哦，真的吗？我挺喜欢蒸桑拿的。

sentences.en: You feel really refreshed afterwards. So, what is a sauna?
sentences.zh: 蒸完之后你会觉得神清气爽。那么，什么是桑拿呢？

sentences.en: Well, a typical sauna is a small wooden room heated with steam to around 80°C.
sentences.zh: 嗯，典型的桑拿房是一个用蒸汽加热到 80°C 左右的小木屋。

sentences.en: It's hot enough to make anyone sweat, but are saunas good for your health as well?
sentences.zh: 这个温度足以让任何人流汗，但桑拿对你的健康也有好处吗？

sentences.en: That's what James Gallagher wanted to find out for BBC Radio 4 programme Inside Health.
sentences.zh: 这就是 James Gallagher 为 BBC Radio 4 节目《Inside Health》想要探寻的答案。

sentences.en: We're seeing what saunas do to the human body.
sentences.zh: 我们正在探究桑拿对人体有什么影响。

sentences.en: They're popping up all over the country with claims that high temperatures boost your health and well-being, but are they all they're cracked up to be?
sentences.zh: 全国各地都冒出了桑拿房，声称高温能促进健康和福祉，但它们真的像人们吹捧的那么好吗？

sentences.en: James wants to find out if saunas are all they're cracked up to be.
sentences.zh: James 想要弄清楚桑拿是不是真的像人们吹捧的那么好。

sentences.en: He means, "Are they as good as people say?" And that's exactly what we'll be finding out in this episode, along with some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，“它们真的像人们说的那么好吗？”这正是我们本期节目要探讨的内容，同时还会学习一些有用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, you can practise all the new vocabulary from this episode with the quiz and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上通过测验和工作表来练习本期节目的所有新词汇。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 不过现在我有一个问题要问你，Georgie。

sentences.en: The word sauna comes from the Finnish language, but what does it mean?
sentences.zh: “sauna”（桑拿）这个词来自芬兰语，但它是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: Does it mean: a) sweat, b) hot water, or c) bathhouse?
sentences.zh: 它的意思是：a) 汗水，b) 热水，还是 c) 澡堂？

sentences.en: Ooh, I'm going to guess c) bathhouse. OK.
sentences.zh: 哦，我猜是 c) 澡堂。好吧。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out if you're right at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们会在节目最后看看你是否答对了。

sentences.en: In recent winters, saunas have grown in popularity in the UK.
sentences.zh: 在最近的几个冬天里，桑拿在英国变得越来越受欢迎。

sentences.en: BBC reporter James Gallagher met some people going to Môr A Sawna, a beach sauna in South Wales.
sentences.zh: BBC 记者 James Gallagher 遇到了一些去 Môr A Sawna 的人，那是南威尔士海滩上的一个桑拿房。

sentences.en: He asked them why they love saunas so much.
sentences.zh: 他问他们为什么这么喜欢蒸桑拿。

sentences.en: Hello everyone! Hello! Who loves a sauna?
sentences.zh: 大家好！你好！谁喜欢蒸桑拿？

sentences.en: Me! Tell me why. Speaker 1 Ah, it's just so relaxing.
sentences.zh: 我！告诉我为什么。发言者 1：啊，就是太让人放松了。

sentences.en: It just makes you feel at ease. Speaker 2 It's also great for relaxing muscles if you're tense or anything like that at all.
sentences.zh: 它就是能让你感到轻松自在。发言者 2：如果你感到紧张或有类似情况，它对放松肌肉也很有好处。

sentences.en: Speaker 3 Yeah, I always love coming down here when I'm a bit stressed out, and by the time that I'm finished, I feel like I've completely reset.
sentences.zh: 发言者 3：是的，当我有点压力过大时，我总是喜欢来这里，等我蒸完之后，我觉得自己完全重置了。

sentences.en: It's wonderful. The first speaker says saunas make her feel at ease – a phrase meaning comfortable and relaxed.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。第一位发言者说桑拿让她感到“at ease”——这个短语的意思是舒适和放松。

sentences.en: And the next speaker thinks saunas are great if you feel tense – an adjective meaning worried and unable to relax.
sentences.zh: 下一位发言者认为，如果你感到“tense”（紧张）——一个表示焦虑且无法放松的形容词，那么桑拿会很棒。

sentences.en: Saunas make the final speaker feel like she's reset.
sentences.zh: 桑拿让最后一位发言者觉得她“reset”（重置）了。

sentences.en: You might already know the word reset to mean turning a computer off and on again when it's not working, but used in connection with a person, reset means to start again after a rest, so that you feel better about life.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经知道“reset”这个词是指电脑死机时关机并重新启动，但当用于人时，“reset”意味着在休息后重新开始，从而让你对生活感觉更好。

sentences.en: So, it seems saunas do help people feel better, but is there actual medical evidence that it's good for us?
sentences.zh: 所以，桑拿似乎确实能让人感觉更好，但有没有实际的医学证据表明它对我们有好处呢？

sentences.en: Here's James Gallagher again, speaking with Professor Damian Bailey, an expert in human physiology for BBC Radio 4 programme Inside Health.
sentences.zh: 下面是 James Gallagher 再次与人体生理学专家 Damian Bailey 教授的对话，该节目是 BBC Radio 4 的《Inside Health》。

sentences.en: When we start to connect this to the arguments around health benefits, is there a health benefit to going in the sauna?
sentences.zh: 当我们开始把这与关于健康益处的争论联系起来时，蒸桑拿对健康有益吗？

sentences.en: Yeah. I mean, I looked at the research really closely.
sentences.zh: 有的。我是说，我非常仔细地研究了相关研究。

sentences.en: I was fascinated by the evidence – huge benefits.
sentences.zh: 我被这些证据迷住了——巨大的益处。

sentences.en: I mean really huge benefits. And it's cultural, of course.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的是巨大的益处。当然，这也是一种文化。

sentences.en: Five million people in Finland – 90% of them use saunas.
sentences.zh: 芬兰有五百万人口——其中 90% 的人蒸桑拿。

sentences.en: Maybe we should be copying what the Finns do, because there's a 40% reduction in all-cause mortality with the sauna-goers.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该效仿芬兰人的做法，因为经常蒸桑拿的人全因死亡率降低了 40%。

sentences.en: Now, this is what we would call observational data, but it's based on thousands and thousands of sauna-goers.
sentences.zh: 现在，这就是我们所说的观察性数据，但它是基于成千上万个蒸桑拿的人的数据。

sentences.en: These are observational data sets, so we really do need what we call RCTs – randomised controlled trials – so everything, just as you've mentioned there, everything is absolutely controlled.
sentences.zh: 这些是观察性数据集，所以我们确实需要所谓的 RCT——随机对照试验——这样一切，就像你刚才提到的，一切都是绝对受控的。

sentences.en: But we can't turn our noses up at the current data – the observational data.
sentences.zh: 但我们不能对现有的数据——即观察性数据——嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: Damian discusses the evidence from Finland, a country where 90% of the population are regular sauna-goers, and it's impressive – a 40% reduction in deaths from all causes.
sentences.zh: Damian 讨论了来自芬兰的证据，在这个国家，90% 的人口经常蒸桑拿，而且结果令人印象深刻——全因死亡率降低了 40%。

sentences.en: But it's important to remember that this is based on observational data – information collected from watching people's natural behaviour and not from controlled medical trials.
sentences.zh: 但重要的是要记住，这是基于观察性数据——即通过观察人们的自然行为收集的信息，而不是来自受控的医学试验。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, this observational data is based on evidence from thousands and thousands of Finns over many years.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这些观察性数据是基于多年来成千上万芬兰人的证据。

sentences.en: That's why Damian thinks we shouldn't turn our noses up at it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么 Damian 认为我们不应该对此嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: We shouldn't reject it simply because we think it's not good enough for us.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该仅仅因为觉得它不够好而拒绝它。

sentences.en: Well, all this talk about saunas has made me want to give it another try, but not before you reveal the answer to your question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 好吧，说了这么多关于桑拿的话题，让我想再试一次，但在这之前，Neil，你得先公布你问题的答案。

sentences.en: I asked you what the Finnish word sauna means.
sentences.zh: 我问过你芬兰语单词“sauna”是什么意思。

sentences.en: Is it: a) sweat, b) hot water, or c) bathhouse?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 汗水，b) 热水，还是 c) 澡堂？

sentences.en: And I said bathhouse. Am I right? You are absolutely correct.
sentences.zh: 我说是澡堂。我答对了吗？你完全正确。

sentences.en: Well done! Yay! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this episode.
sentences.zh: 做得好！耶！好了。让我们复习一下我们在本期节目中学到的词汇。

sentences.en: If something is not all it's cracked up to be, it isn't as good as people say.
sentences.zh: 如果某件事“not all it's cracked up to be”，意思就是它没有人们说的那么好。

sentences.en: When someone's at ease, they feel comfortable and unstressed, whereas a tense person is worried and unable to relax.
sentences.zh: 当某人“at ease”时，他们感到舒适且没有压力，而一个“tense”的人则感到焦虑且无法放松。

sentences.en: When someone resets, they start again after a rest which has made them feel better about life.
sentences.zh: 当某人“resets”时，他们在休息后重新开始，这让他们对生活感觉更好。

sentences.en: Observational data is information collected from watching people's natural behaviour without interfering in it.
sentences.zh: “Observational data”（观察性数据）是指在不进行干预的情况下，通过观察人们的自然行为收集的信息。

sentences.en: And finally, if you turn your nose up at something, you reject it because you think it's not good enough for you.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你对某事“turn your nose up at”（嗤之以鼻），你就会因为觉得它不够好而拒绝它。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. But if you want to improve your English with more trending topics and useful vocabulary, you'll find plenty on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了。但如果你想通过更多热门话题和实用词汇来提高英语水平，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到很多内容。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 我们很快再见。不过现在，要说再见了。

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
